rows.statement: Grow Heritage Pure Milk volume share in core South India (TG, AP, KA, TN) by winning switchers from loose milk and rival packs.
rows.measure: +X pts volume share vs baseline — Heritage to set X and baseline [unverified]

rows.statement: Convert daily buyers of loose/unbranded and rival branded milk to a Heritage Pure Milk daily habit, and lift repeat frequency among trialists.
rows.measure: Household penetration in core markets + repeat-purchase rate — targets to be set against panel data Heritage holds

rows.statement: Make 'purity you can trust every morning' the reason families choose Heritage — land the unbroken cold-chain proof and the everyday-strength belief.
rows.measure: Prompted brand consideration + agreement with 'purest everyday milk' among core-market milk buyers — brand-tracker to baseline
rows.by_when: tracked quarterly from launch, read at 12 months

rows.audience: Loose-milk households in core South India — the daily buyer (often the woman running the kitchen) who takes milk from a local vendor or dairy booth, boils it each morning, trusts 'fresh and local'
rows.believes_now: Believes loose milk is fresher and cheaper because it comes straight from a nearby source, and that packaged milk is 'older' or watered down. Does not see a hygiene or purity risk in her current habit — the vendor is known and trusted. This is the largest switchable volume pool and the one the marketing objective names first. She is beaten by proof, not by warmth: the unbroken cold-chain clock directly attacks the 'loose is fresher' belief.

rows.audience: Rival branded-milk households — families already buying Amul, Nandini, Dodla or Arokya packs on daily delivery or from general trade
rows.believes_now: Already accepts packaged milk as safe and convenient, so the purity/hygiene argument is table stakes here and does not move them. Chooses on habit, availability and price. To switch them you must offer a reason beyond 'also safe' — that Heritage milk is richer, more nourishing, the strength the family runs on. Emotional pillar does the work; leading with functional proof only confirms what they already believe about their current brand.

rows.audience: Aspirational young families and new parents in metro/tier-1 core markets — recently formed households, first child, actively upgrading what they buy for the home
rows.believes_now: Actively questioning what is 'good enough' for a child and willing to pay up for reassurance, but not yet loyal to any dairy brand. Reads purity as care. Smaller in volume than ranks 1 and 2 but high repeat value and premium-tolerant — the segment that most readily pays for 'won't compromise'. The nourishment-for-a-growing-family argument lands hardest here.

rows.audience: Existing Heritage buyers at risk of lapsing to loose milk on price — current daily customers whose loyalty is soft
rows.believes_now: Buys Heritage today but treats milk as a commodity and would drift back to a cheaper loose vendor on a bad week. Needs the reason-to-stay made concrete and repeatable. Retention volume, not new volume — cheaper to hold than to win. The cold-chain proof reminds them what the price gap actually buys.

rows.occasion: The pre-dawn boil / first-coffee ritual — the daily moment the standing-order decision is anchored to, before any switch is asked for
rows.channels: Cold-chain clock film (TV, lead) + 15s vertical cutdowns (digital-video) + steel-vessel OOH — proof and reach only; no conversion push yet
rows.hands_over: A believed purity claim and 'roz subah' salience, so Phase 2's trial ask lands on households who already trust the cold never breaks

rows.occasion: The daily buying window — pre-dawn boil / first coffee — where loose-milk and rival-brand intent is live and a standing order is actually placed
rows.channels: Doorstep sampling + first-week trial (home-delivery, activation lead this phase) + GT crate/booth conversion + morning-drive radio + brand/category search — reach channels stay live underneath
rows.hands_over: A base of standing daily orders and new GT outlets handling, so Phase 3 has subscribers to hold and advocates to activate

rows.occasion: The nourishment moment — feeding a growing family, when new parents and rank-2/3 households reconsider what milk goes in the glass
rows.channels: Nourishment-for-a-growing-family films (social, reach) targeting new parents/switchers + continued search + home-delivery trial
rows.hands_over: A second wave of trial from the emotional pillar, feeding the same standing-order and subscription funnel

rows.occasion: The daily repeat pour — the ritual once you're the household's milk, where retention and referral are won or lost every morning
rows.channels: Subscriber CRM (advocacy) — retention nudges, cold-chain reminder, win-back, referral + quick-commerce listing for top-up demand
rows.hands_over: Retained subscribers and referrals that lower Phase 2's future CPA; feeds back into the next annual build cycle
